frequency_question: How often do such threatened sector-specific tariffs actually take effect on the scheduled deadline rather than being delayed, withdrawn, or replaced by a negotiated agreement?
membership_rule: Includes: explicit tariff threats with specific implementation dates targeting a specific sector in Canada or Mexico under USMCA/NAFTA. Excludes: broad global baseline tariffs (like Section 232 steel/aluminum globally) or threats without a specific implementation date.

cases.name: US threatened 25% tariffs on all Mexican imports over immigration (June 2019)
US threatened 5% escalating to 25% tariffs on Canada/Mexico regarding steel/aluminum removal negotiations (2018)
US threatened 100% secondary tariffs on Canadian digital services tax disputes or trade retaliation

coverage_note: 3 named; represents the complete population of high-stakes immediate bilateral tariff ultimatums within the USMCA/NAFTA framework over the past decade.
known_gaps: Borderline threats communicated privately or retracted before formal scheduling are excluded by the formal announcement rule.
skeleton: Threatened bilateral trade ultimatums with immediate deadlines against integrated partners yielding implementation vs negotiated climbdown.
multiplier: 1 hit out of 3 major distinct ultimatum episodes
validity_reason: Relies on the current presidential administration's negotiating style and institutional framework, which remains stable through the current term.
